rows.source: UKHSA polio surveillance and containment
rows.verified: National guidance covers surveillance, investigation and management of suspected polio cases.

rows.source: UKHSA polio surveillance and containment
rows.verified: The guidance supports the UK commitment to the WHO global polio eradication programme.

rows.source: UKHSA polio surveillance and containment
rows.verified: The national polio framework includes enhanced enterovirus surveillance.

rows.source: UKHSA polio surveillance and containment
rows.verified: Suspected acute flaccid paralysis is subject to public-health surveillance.

rows.source: UKHSA polio surveillance and containment
rows.verified: Public-health management includes consideration of post-exposure prophylaxis.

rows.source: UKHSA polio surveillance and containment
rows.verified: Appropriate clinical and laboratory samples are required to confirm infection.

rows.source: UKHSA polio surveillance and containment
rows.verified: Containment requirements apply to storage and use of polioviruses.

rows.source: UKHSA polio surveillance and containment
rows.verified: The guidelines are intended for public-health professionals and laboratory staff.

rows.source: UKHSA polio surveillance and containment
rows.verified: Polio risk depends on virus type, immunity, travel or environmental exposure, sanitation, surveillance and contact context.

rows.source: UKHSA polio surveillance and containment
rows.verified: Polio evidence is case-, virus-, sample-, contact- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.

rows.source: UKHSA tetanus wound and case management
rows.verified: Debrided tissue is the preferred specimen for tetanus testing and debridement also has therapeutic value.

rows.source: UKHSA tetanus wound and case management
rows.verified: A negative PCR or culture result does not exclude tetanus.

rows.source: UKHSA tetanus wound and case management
rows.verified: A pre-immunoglobulin tetanus antibody level below 0.1 IU/mL can support the diagnosis.

rows.source: UKHSA tetanus wound and case management
rows.verified: An antibody level at or above 0.1 IU/mL does not exclude tetanus.

rows.source: UKHSA tetanus wound and case management
rows.verified: Point-of-care antibody tests are not recommended for diagnosing suspected tetanus.

rows.source: UKHSA tetanus wound and case management
rows.verified: Clinical management can include debridement, antimicrobials, immunoglobulin, vaccination and supportive care.

rows.source: UKHSA tetanus wound and case management
rows.verified: Early intravenous immunoglobulin treatment can be lifesaving in suspected clinical tetanus.

rows.source: UKHSA tetanus wound and case management
rows.verified: Five appropriately spaced tetanus vaccine doses are considered to provide lifelong protection.

rows.source: UKHSA tetanus wound and case management
rows.verified: Tetanus risk depends on wound type, contamination, tissue damage, immunisation history, time to treatment and host factors.

rows.source: UKHSA tetanus wound and case management
rows.verified: Tetanus evidence is wound-, patient-, immunisation-, treatment- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level disease probability.
